studies.task: Each participant completed three rounds of one randomly assigned task: unusual uses for an object (AUT), ten unrelated words (DAT), or a word connecting three cues (RAT).

ai_tool.name: Unnamed LLM assistant; low-randomness temperature 0.1 or high-randomness temperature 1.2
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 1 (printed p. 1770), Abstract; PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1771), Sections III.A-B; PDF p. 5 (printed p. 1774), Figure 1. No model, provider, or release year is named for the experimental assistant.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Mean of all pairwise cosine distances among a participant's AUT responses, computed with spaCy en_core_web_md embeddings. The raw distance scale runs from 0 (identical meaning) to 2 (opposite meanings). This measures variety within a participant, coded flexibility rather than diversity across people. The paper does not state whether responses are pooled across rounds or scored separately (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1771, Section III.C).

regression.model: Regression on HighRandomness and NoAI indicators, with the low-randomness condition as the omitted reference, adjusting for duration_seconds and AI_used. The extracted NoAI coefficient is AUT_NoAI minus AUT_Low (control minus treatment). Estimator, regression N, observation unit, and standard-error method are not stated.

PDF p. 3 (printed p. 1772), Section IV Results, regression specification
sources.quote: Specifically, we regressed each of the outcome variables of interest on the experimental condition, controlling for time spent on the task and whether AI was actually used.

sources.locator: PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1771), Section III.C Measures, semantic-distance scale
sources.quote: Distance values range from 0 (identical semantic meaning) to 2 (opposite meanings), with typical values between 0 and 1.

sources.locator: PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1771), Section III.C Measures, participant response sets
sources.quote: For each participant's set of responses, we generated embedding vectors for all responses using spaCy, calculated pairwise cosine similarity between all response vectors, and converted similarities to distances (distance = 1 − similarity).

estimates.notes: The coefficient and standard error are transcribed with their printed signs and precision. The printed NoAI coefficient is the reverse of the named AI-versus-no-AI contrast; its sign has not been changed. Any later effect calculation must account for this coefficient orientation. The model adjusts for actual AI use after assignment, so the condition coefficient is not an unadjusted intention-to-treat effect. No exact p-value, arm outcome means, outcome SDs, confidence intervals, or standardized effect are printed for this contrast. The absence of a significance star is not converted into a p-value. Table I arm counts are retained in the study record; the paper does not give counts for this regression, so the estimate counts are null. The scoring description refers to participant response sets, but the regression could use participant or participant-round observations; unit and se_basis are null because this is not established. Standard errors are printed, so se_basis is not coded not_reported.

sources.locator: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 1772), Section V Discussion, second paragraph
sources.quote: For convergent thinking tasks such as the RAT, LLMs (irrespective of their level of randomness in the 0.1- 1.2 range) increase accuracy (on average, from 45 to 55%, p < .05).

sources.locator: PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1771), Section III.C Measures, RAT accuracy definition
sources.quote: The accuracy score was calculated as the number of correct responses divided by the total number of problems attempted.

estimates.notes: Full-sample AI-availability comparison, kept separate from the subsequent AI-user subsample result. Percentages are recorded as printed, without conversion to proportions or calculation of a difference. No SD, SE, confidence interval, test statistic, test name, standardized effect, or analysis-specific count is printed with this contrast. The analyzed cell counts appear separately in the study record; they are not assumed to be counts for the unspecified test. The unit and the basis of the p-value are not stated, so unit and se_basis are null. Section IV says p-values for this and all following results are Holm-adjusted, which covers this later Discussion result by its wording. RAT is a convergent outcome and is not pooled with creativity effects.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Mean pairwise cosine distance among the words a participant generated, using the same spaCy en_core_web_md procedure and raw distance scale (0 to 2) as AUT. The paper does not state whether each round is scored separately or the words are pooled across rounds. Within-participant variety is coded flexibility (PDF pp. 2-3, printed pp. 1771-1772, Section III.C).

estimates.notes: Eligible outcome and full-sample condition contrast retained with null statistics. Section IV says that no DAT coefficients were significant and therefore omits them; this is not evidence of a zero effect or an exact p-value. The contrast follows the shared experimental-condition specification and the contrasts mapped in the reconciled screening form. No arm levels, SDs, coefficient, SE, test statistic, p-value, interval, or standardized effect are printed. The study record retains the Table I cell counts; no DAT regression N or observation unit is supplied. The scoring description concerns a participant's own words, not similarity between different participants. It is unclear whether rounds were pooled. There is no reported uncertainty for this DAT contrast.

open_items: No performance-outcome SDs, confidence intervals, or standardized effects are printed. Full-sample AUT and DAT arm means are absent; only the pooled AI-versus-no-AI RAT percentages are reported as full-sample arm levels.

The regression sample sizes, participant versus participant-round observation unit, estimator, and standard-error method are not stated. Do not assume that the Table I cell sizes establish the N for each fitted model.

se_basis is null for the printed regressions and the pooled RAT p-value because the independence unit cannot be confirmed. The vocabulary lacks an unknown-basis value distinct from not_reported; not_reported would incorrectly imply that the regressions print no uncertainty. Do not pool these uncertainties without clarification.

The NoAI regression coefficients are printed for no AI minus low randomness. They are stored without sign reversal although the named treatment arm is the low-randomness AI arm; downstream calculations must respect the coefficient direction described in regression.model and notes.

Tables II and III adjust for AI_used after assignment; their condition coefficients are not unadjusted intention-to-treat effects. Unadjusted assigned-arm AUT and RAT coefficients with participant-level uncertainty are not supplied.
Whether AUT and DAT distance scores pool all task rounds or are computed separately is not stated. This also prevents confirmation of regression independence.
The DAT regression coefficients are omitted because none was significant. No numerical DAT result can be reconstructed from that statement.

The paper reports recruited and retained participants but does not give the number randomized or when exclusions occurred relative to assignment. Allocation ratios and exclusions by cell are not given.
The experimental LLM model, provider, and release year, participant countries, and any preregistration are not stated.

RAT answer accuracy does not fit any measure code exactly. automated_score is the screening form's explicit placeholder; the paper reports neither a creativity-scoring model nor the procedure used to judge correctness.
Section IV says this and all following p-values are Holm-adjusted, while the table notes only give significance-star thresholds. Whether those stars also use adjusted p-values is unclear.
The citation and retrieval records identify an IEEE version of record with different pagination. Page-by-page identity with this saved MIPRO copy remains unverified.
notes: Extractor B, 2026-10-10. Read the complete six-page PDF and all lines of its markdown conversion, including references; inspected Tables I-III and Figure 1. No appendix or supplement is present or referenced, and no separate supplement matching this paper is on file. The figure is a platform screenshot and contains no outcome statistics. The statistic inventory consists of the condition-coefficient/SE pairs in Tables II-III, the pooled RAT percentages and p-value in Section V, the omitted DAT results, and the noneligible subgroup/correlation/covariate statistics individually listed in not_extracted. One factorial randomized experiment is retained as S1, with task-specific arms and five outcome definitions matching the screening form. AUT and DAT measure variation within a participant, so they are flexibility outcomes under with_ai, not across_people diversity. RAT is convergent and remains outside the creativity pool. No after_ai output is reported. PDF p. 3 (printed p. 1772), Section III.D reports "We conducted the study in December 2025" and "We then proceeded to recruit 960 participants"; this recruitment count is not substituted for n_randomized. Table I counts are recorded without computing task or contrast totals. Estimate counts are null when the paper does not tie a count to the reported analysis; all printed retained cell counts remain in the study record. No standard errors, differences, standardized effects, sample-size sums, or p-values have been derived. All recorded coefficients retain their printed signs, and percentages retain their printed units.
